name: Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
tagline: Ayyappa's hill shrine where Devaprasnam (prasna) and jyotisha shape big ritual and administrative choices
summary: Sabarimala is Kerala’s largest Ayyappa pilgrimage site; its multi-day Ashtamangala Devaprasnam (prasna) and Jyotisha consultations routinely guide temple ritual timing, priestly appointments and…
description: Sabarimala is the hill shrine of Lord Ayyappa (Sree Dharma Sastha) in Pathanamthitta district, visited by millions during Mandala-Makaravilakku season and throughout the year. The temple sits inside the Western Ghats and follows long-standing Kerala temple usages.

Beyond the daily worship and the 41‑day vratham tradition of pilgrims, Sabarimala’s large-scale ritual and administrative decisions are regularly informed by Ashtamangala Devaprasnam — a formal, multi-day horary-astrology ritual led by expert Kerala jyotishis. Devaprasnam reports (prasnacharthu) historically advise the temple’s thanthri and the Travancore Devaswom Board on matters from structural works to priestly rights.

Devaprasnam at Sabarimala is part of a living temple governance culture: findings are recorded and, in several court rulings and administrative orders, have been treated as determining the ‘devahitham’ (the deity’s revealed will) that the Board and temple authorities must respect. Visitors encounter a landscape of strong ritual protocol, year-long maintenance and coordinated administration under the Travancore Devaswom Board.

For travellers and students of ritual, Sabarimala offers a chance to see how astrology (prasna) and traditional priestly authority continue to shape one of India’s largest pilgrimages; public access to ritual deliberations is limited and event timings change, so confirm details before you plan to attend any prasna ceremony.
highlights: Major pilgrimage centre of Lord Ayyappa with millions of devotees each year
Ashtamangala Devaprasnam (devaprasnam) — multi‑day horary ritual that informs temple decisions
Thanthri (hereditary priest) and Travancore Devaswom Board implement prasna findings
Mandala (approx. mid‑Nov to Dec) and Makaravilakku seasons govern opening and large pilgrim flows
Pathinettam padi (18 sacred steps) and traditional 41‑day vratham are central to pilgrimage practice

sections.heading: Background
body: Devaprasnam (also written Deva Prasnam or Ashtamangala Devaprasnam) is a specialised branch of Kerala jyotisha (horary astrology). In temple use it is a ritual inquiry — often lasting several days — led by senior prasna vidwans and ritual specialists to discern the deity’s will about temple health, worship, rites, installations and disputes.

At Sabarimala the Devaprasnam tradition sits beside hereditary thanthric authority and statutory administration by the Travancore Devaswom Board. Kerala High Court judgments and special-commissioner reports over the years record that Devaprasnam findings (the prasnacharthu) are submitted to the thanthri and the board and are treated as the deity’s directive (devahitham) that must be given effect.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Pilgrims come for darshan following the customary 41‑day vratham, carrying the irumudi kettu and observing the dress and conduct rules of the pilgrimage. The hill shrine’s core experiences are the trek to the sabarimala sannidhanam, the Pathinettampadi (eighteen sacred steps) and the darshan of Lord Ayyappa.

Devaprasnam itself is not a regular public spectacle — it is a formal, often invited ceremony conducted by expert astrologers and priestly panels. When a Devaprasnam is scheduled (for matters such as consecrations, repairs, priest appointments or when anomalies are suspected), the findings are presented to temple authorities; ordinary pilgrims typically learn about outcomes after the event rather than attend the deliberations.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Sabarimala opens for major seasonal periods (Mandala — roughly mid‑November to late December — and Makaravilakku/Makar Sankranti on 14 January) and for specified days each Malayalam month. Exact opening and festival dates vary year to year; confirm current schedules with official Travancore Devaswom Board channels before you travel.

If you wish to learn about Devaprasnam practice, look for public reports, news coverage and Devaswom notifications after a Devaprasnam; do not expect routine public attendance. Respect temple protocols — observe dress codes, photography rules and the sanctity of ritual spaces. Confirm event access and timings with the Travancore Devaswom Board or official temple announcements.

latest.text: Kerala High Court judgment in W.A.1021/2016 records that a Devaprasnam ‘charthu’ was used by the Travancore Devaswom Board in deciding Thanthri appointment — court documents note that Devaprasnam findings are implemented by the Board.

Kerala High Court – SSCR No.24 of 2025 (Sabarimala Special Commissioner report) details procedures for selection of melsanthis and underlines the continuing role of thanthris and customary practices in Sabarimala administration.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Pilgrimage season: Mandala (approx. mid‑November to late December) and Makaravilakku (mid‑January); low‑season months are quieter — confirm dates before you go.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Nearest road access is from Pamba (drive or bus from Pathanamthitta/Thiruvananthapuram/Kottayam). Trek route begins at Pamba; nearest major railway station: Chengannur / Thiruvalla; nearest airport: Thiruvananthapuram. Confirm local transport and seasonal restrictions before travel.
etiquette: Respect ritual protocols and the thanthri’s authority; do not assume you can witness Devaprasnam ceremonies.
Check official Travancore Devaswom Board or temple announcements for festival dates, priest selections or special prasna outcomes — these change year to year.
Pilgrims usually observe a 41‑day vratham; follow local guidance on dress, food and conduct (confirm current requirements before you go).
Avoid unauthorised guides and unofficial claims about prasna results; rely on published Devaswom or court documents for official decisions.
